GitHub Issue:
Post Date: 2019-01-07T20:06:40Z
Current Date: April 4 2025
Title: Extract<keyof T, string> is not assignable to K extends Extract<keyof T, string> when used as K[]
Description: **TypeScript Version:**  3.3.0-dev.20190105

<!-- Search terms you tried before logging this (so others can find this issue more easily) -->
**Search Terms:** keyof string array, K extends Extract<keyof T, string>

**Code**

Using a generic `K extends Extract<keyof T, string>` generic definition does not work:

```ts
function copyAllExcept<T, K extends Extract<keyof T, string>>(target: any, source: T, skip: K[]) {
    for (const key in source) {
        if (source[key] != null && !skip.includes(key)) {
            target[key] = source[key];
        }
    }
}
```
Error at the `!skip.includes(key)` part:

Argument of type 'Extract<keyof T, string>' is not assignable to parameter of type 'K'.
  Type 'string & keyof T' is not assignable to type 'K'.
    Type 'string' is not assignable to type 'K'.
      Type 'string' is not assignable to type 'K'.


Using `Array<Extract<keyof T, string>>` directly as the argument definition does work though:

```ts
function copyAllExcept<T>(target: any, source: T, skip: Array<Extract<keyof T, string>>) {
    for (const key in source) {
        if (source[key] != null && !skip.includes(key)) {
            target[key] = source[key];
        }
    }
}
```
